claim: In mice performing a reaction-time random-dot motion task, a bounded accumulator with drift variability and fast guesses predicted held-out control-trial choices and response times better than a tested rapid-forgetting model, in a comparison not yet shown to identify rapid forgetting, whereas brief motion pulses moved choices far more than either control-fitted model predicted, which left the temporal weighting of evidence unresolved.

Relative ranking of two misspecified implementations; 4/10 mice do not distinguish them; no rapid-forgetting-generated recovery of the comparison (F1a pending). Conditional replacements and fallback in spine.md 'Conditional thesis'. Temporal weighting undetermined, not shown flat. 'Far more than either model predicted' needs ledger ids for the original predicted pulse effects [MISSING: number ids, see C010].

claim: Trained mice performed the reaction-time random-dot direction task: choices followed signed coherence, and response times and the probability of no response by 5 s varied with coherence.
note: Performance only (D001 item 2); no learning or training claim. Summary performance numbers (e.g. accuracy at 100%) are not in the ledger; add if the text needs them. 5 s is an analysis cutoff.

note: Discussion synthesis. Must not attribute the pulse mismatch to a sensory, decision or response stage. Strengthens to identification wording only if F1a recovers both generators (spine conditional thesis).
